name: Alternaria leaf spot
summary: A laboratory-confirmed Cannabis leaf-spot disease. Brown lesions with yellow halos are compatible with Alternaria, but that appearance overlaps several hemp pathogens and must not be treated as species-level image ground truth.
indicators: Small spots enlarge into brown irregular lesions with light yellow halos
Lesion centers may become fragile or perforated as disease advances
Multiple lesions can expand and merge on affected foliage
exclusions: Pycnidia strongly support a Septoria differential
Sooty underside conidial masses support Pseudocercospora
Round white-centered lesions with melanized conidiophores support Cercospora
No pathogen evidence is present and spray or contact injury maps to the lesion distribution

progression.description: Spots enlarge into irregular brown lesions with pale yellow halos.
Lesions expand, coalesce, and centers may perforate.

confirmation: For species-level diagnosis use culture and/or validated molecular identification from representative lesions.
Photograph both surfaces and lesion distribution and preserve a sample before treatment.
immediateActions: Separate heavily affected propagation material and reduce avoidable leaf wetness while diagnosis is pending.
correctivePlan: Use a disease-management plan appropriate to the confirmed pathogen and production setting.
Remove heavily diseased debris when appropriate and monitor new lesions.
prevention: Avoid moving symptomatic plant material between clean areas.
Use sanitation and irrigation practices that limit prolonged leaf wetness.
warnings: Brown spots with yellow halos are not Alternaria-specific.
The primary report was one regional disease occurrence; prevalence varies by environment and production system.

sources.title: First Report of Leaf Spot on Industrial Hemp (Cannabis sativa) Caused by Alternaria alternata in China
supportedClaims: Industrial hemp leaf spots began as small spots and developed into brown irregular lesions with light yellow halos; lesion centers could perforate as disease advanced.
The isolate was identified as Alternaria alternata by morphology and multilocus molecular evidence, and inoculated healthy hemp developed similar lesions while controls remained asymptomatic.
Re-isolation from inoculated plants fulfilled Koch postulates, so the record supports an organism-confirmed Cannabis leaf-spot diagnosis rather than visual similarity alone.
